services.openssh.enable.riskNote: Enables remote access: opens port 22 in the firewall. Key-only: password and keyboard-interactive logins and root login are turned off, so add your public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys first.

nexusos.secureBoot.enable.summary: Secure Boot: sign the start-up menu and kernels with this computer's own keys
nexusos.secureBoot.enable.riskNote: Changes how the computer starts: keys are made on this computer and the start-up menu and kernels are signed with them, and the start-up menu's editor is turned off. Nothing in the firmware changes yet; Settings, About then guides you through putting the keys in the firmware (Microsoft's stay, so Windows still starts) and switching Secure Boot on.

nexusos.developer.virtualMachines.enable.summary: Virtual machines: KVM with libvirt, QEMU and virt-manager

nexusos.sharing.enable.summary: Share folders with other computers on this network (read-only)

nexusos.fingerprint.enable.summary: Fingerprint for the lock screen and approvals

nexusos.malwareScan.enable.summary: Scan files for viruses on demand (ClamAV)

nexusos.hibernate.enable.summary: Hibernate: save everything to the disk and turn off

nexusos.guest.enable.summary: A guest account with no password, wiped at each log out

nexusos.hardware.broadcomWifi.enable.summary: Broadcom's own Wi-Fi driver, for chips Linux has no driver for
nexusos.hardware.broadcomWifi.enable.riskNote: Broadcom's driver is closed and no longer maintained, and has known flaws that someone nearby could use to take over the computer over Wi-Fi (CVE-2019-9501, CVE-2019-9502). Use it only until you can add a supported USB or M.2 Wi-Fi card, and keep it off where you do not trust the networks around you.

packages.summary: Install a package from the system's pinned nixpkgs into environment.systemPackages
